title: On the Tension between Byzantine Robustness and No-Attack Accuracy in Distributed Learning
summary: Theorem 4.6 states a false finite-time guarantee; the core lower-bound proof contains invalid case reasoning. Corrected guarantees and core aggregation results survive.
limitations: No author repository, raw experiments or later correction inspected.
Separate supplement availability unresolved; full Appendix A is in the original.
No empirical reproduction or author-code execution.
Inherited external constants and broad priority claim not independently verified.

claim.location: PDF page 6 Theorem 4.6 first display; page 21 Appendix A.7 after Equation (30)
claim.text: Average squared gradient is at most 2L[F*-F(wT)]/T + epsilon G^2.

assumptions: n=3, f=1, scalar median, (1,1)-robust and epsilon=1/2 accurate.
F1=w^2/2; F2=F3=w^2/2-w; L=mu=1; F*=-2/9; global gradient heterogeneity G^2=2/9.
w0=0; eta=1/L=1; T=1; no Byzantine workers.
problems.check: Exact rational evaluation and independent descent/telescoping argument.
problems.result: w1=1; left side 4/9; printed right side 0.
counterevidence: Appendix A.7 contains the correct F(w0)-F(wT) telescoping bound.
Correcting to F(w0)-F* preserves the asymptotic epsilon G^2 floor and does not refute the PL bound.
problems.impact: A false principal finite-time guarantee in the core convergence/tightness contribution.
problems.correction: Use 2L[F(w0)-F*]/T + epsilon G^2; full proof supplied from the valid one-step inequality.
problems.core_dependency: Main convergence guarantee for the claimed robustness/accuracy relationship.
problems.severity_rationale: Major: median example with n=3,f=1 satisfies hypotheses but yields squared gradient 4/9 above printed RHS zero.

acceptance_check.scope: Correct telescoping numerator uses F(w0)-F(wT); this does not certify all amended theorem variants.

claim.location: PDF page 21 Appendix A.6 case (iii); related periodic-case steps on pages 20-21
claim.text: For every initialization and eta above the threshold, wt tends to positive infinity, establishing the lower bound by divergence.

assumptions: Same admissible quadratic construction; eta=3>2; w0=1.
problems.result: wt=1 at all times; gradient squared 1/9 and objective gap 1/18 do not diverge. The theorem conclusion remains true.
counterevidence: The robust-majority construction itself is valid.
A complete fixed-point/stable/periodic/unstable case argument restores the claimed lower bound.
problems.impact: Invalid reasoning used to finish an every-initialization, every-positive-step core proof. Not a false-theorem finding.
problems.correction: Separate u=0, |r|<1, r=-1 and r<-1 with u nonzero; use absolute divergence and periodic averages. Full argument included.
problems.core_dependency: Proof of the principal simultaneous late-iterate impossibility claim.
problems.severity_rationale: Major: unconditional divergence statement fails at the fixed point and needs full recurrence/parity cases.

acceptance_check.scope: Explicit recurrence handles fixed/contracting/periodic/divergent cases and recovers the stated arbitrarily-late quantifier; false proof step is still core.

claim.location: PDF page 4 middle-group variance definition and page 5 Equation (7)
claim.text: The middle group variance uses denominator f in the displayed decomposition.

problems.check: Compute full variance and the printed decomposition.
problems.result: 2 versus 14/5; correcting the middle divisor to n-2f restores 2.
counterevidence: Appendix A.3 page 16 uses the correct divisor and proves the theorem.
problems.impact: Local proof-sketch inconsistency; trimmed-mean theorem verified.
problems.correction: Replace 1/f by 1/(n-2f) in the middle-group definition.
problems.severity_rationale: Minor: divisor f should be n-2f; Appendix A.3 uses the correct denominator and supports the intended bound.

acceptance_check.scope: Local formula repair; retain valid weighted variance decomposition.
